narrative.coaching_note: The one change to make next time is to wash your hands with soap and water for 40 seconds after you leave the bedside and before you touch anything outside it. At 0.5 seconds you touched bed rail A with your bare hand, and that contamination moved to call button at 3.4 seconds and then to phone at 6.6 seconds. You missed hand cleaning after the bedside at 5.8 seconds and again at 18.7 seconds after touching call button with your gloved hand, so phone stayed contaminated at the end. Alcohol rub would not clear Norovirus, so use soap and water. Next time, clean your hands with soap and water before you put gloves on, and keep your gloved hand off items like phone outside the bedside.
narrative.audit_summary: Norovirus source bed rail A. Bare hand contacted bed rail A at 0.5s with transfer to bare hand, then to call button at 3.4s and to phone at 6.6s; gloved hand contacted bed rail A at 11.1s after donning at 10.9s. Two Moment 5 opportunities missed at 5.8s (bare hand) and 18.7s (gloved hand); compliance 0/2 overall and 0/2 for Moment 5, with no opportunities for Moments 1, 2, or 4. No hand hygiene performed; for Norovirus alcohol rub is largely ineffective and soap and water is required. Glove use involved donning without prior hygiene and touching phone in healthcare area with gloved hand. Contaminated at end: bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, phone. Disinfect bed rail A, call button, and phone with Use an EPA List G registered disinfectant (effective against norovirus).
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene with soap and water at 5.8 seconds.
